pharm: Substituted benzimidazole that irreversibly inhibits the gastric H+/K+ ATPase (proton pump) in parietal cells, suppressing basal and stimulated acid secretion.
quick: 15-30 mg once daily depending on indication
Take before eating, usually in the morning
Limited human data; use only if clearly needed
Magnesium and B12 on long-term use
summary: Lansoprazole is a proton pump inhibitor used for duodenal and gastric ulcers, H. pylori eradication (in combination), GERD, erosive esophagitis, NSAID-associated ulcers, and pathological hypersecretory conditions including Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. It is taken before eating and works by irreversibly blocking gastric acid secretion.
indications: Active duodenal ulcer and maintenance of healing in adults
Eradication of H. pylori to reduce duodenal ulcer recurrence (combination therapy)
Healing and risk reduction of NSAID-associated gastric ulcer
Symptomatic GERD (adults and children 1 year and older)
Erosive esophagitis: treatment and maintenance of healing
Pathological hypersecretory conditions including Zollinger-Ellison syndrome

dosage.n: Maintenance of healed ulcer: 15 mg once daily

dosage.d: Lansoprazole 30 mg + amoxicillin 1 g + clarithromycin 500 mg, all twice daily
dosage.n: Dual therapy: lansoprazole 30 mg + amoxicillin 1 g, all three times daily for 14 days

dosage.d: 30 mg once daily for up to 8 weeks
dosage.n: NSAID-associated ulcer healing: 30 mg once daily for 8 weeks

dosage.d: Symptomatic GERD 15 mg once daily up to 8 weeks; EE 30 mg once daily up to 8 weeks

admin: Take before eating, usually in the morning
Swallow delayed-release capsules whole; do not chew or crush
Capsule contents may be sprinkled on soft food or given via select methods per label if swallowing is difficult
Complete the full course for ulcer healing and H. pylori eradication
moa: Lansoprazole is a substituted benzimidazole that accumulates in the acidic parietal cell canaliculus where it is converted to the active sulfenamide. This covalently binds and irreversibly inhibits the H+/K+ ATPase, the final step of gastric acid secretion, suppressing both basal and stimulated acid output regardless of stimulus.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to any component of the formulation
relative: Long-term high-dose therapy (fracture, hypomagnesemia, B12 deficiency risk)
Drugs requiring gastric acidity for absorption

preg: Limited human data; no clear major risk signal but adequate controlled studies are lacking. Use only if clearly needed.
lact: Limited data on transfer into milk; weigh maternal need against potential infant exposure.
renal: No dosage adjustment required in renal impairment.
hepatic: Clearance is reduced and AUC increased in hepatic impairment; consider dose reduction in severe impairment.

major: pH-dependent drugs: atazanavir, nelfinavir, ketoconazole, itraconazole, erlotinib (reduced absorption)
interactions.food: Take before eating; food can reduce absorption if taken with meals.
interactions.diagnostics: Elevates serum chromogranin A; may cause false-positive secretin stimulation test.

monitoring: Symptom response and need for continued therapy
Renal function if interstitial nephritis suspected
counsel: Take before eating in the morning
Swallow capsules whole; do not chew or crush
May take days for full symptom relief; complete the prescribed course
Report persistent diarrhea, muscle cramps, or signs of low magnesium on long-term use
Tell your clinician about all other medicines, including HIV drugs
pk: Acid suppression within 1-3 hours; full effect over days
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); protect from moisture
pearls: Effect outlasts plasma half-life due to irreversible pump binding
Best taken before the first meal of the day
Used as part of triple/dual therapy for H. pylori eradication
Reassess long-term use; limit duration to lowest effective level
missed: If a daily dose is missed, take it when remembered the same day; if near the next dose, skip it. Do not double up.
overdose: Lansoprazole is extensively protein-bound and not effectively removed by dialysis. No specific antidote; manage symptomatically and supportively.
